content:
A federal appeals court has upheld qualified immunity for three Laredo police officers sued over a 2021 arrest during the city's COVID-19 curfew, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a district court's grant of immunity to officers Carlos Ibarra and Gerardo Jalomo and Sgt. Roberto Fernandez in a civil-rights suit brought by Ismael Rincon.

The case dates to Feb. 6, 2021, at about 1:29 a.m., when Rincon drove into a vacant parking lot during Laredo's curfew period, which ran from 6 p.m. to 5 a.m. for social activities outside a person's household, with exceptions for business-related activity. Officers who were nearby doing paperwork approached him over a possible curfew violation. According to the Laredo Morning Times, Rincon said he was eating but declined to give further information, his name, or his driver's license. An officer ordered him out of the vehicle and frisked him, finding a holstered weapon on his hip that was later determined to be a pellet gun. After Rincon said he had plenty of other weapons, the officer searched the passenger compartment, and other officers inventoried the vehicle, finding several firearms and ammunition. The vehicle was towed, Rincon was arrested on an unlawful-carrying charge, and he was cited for violating the curfew and for failing to identify himself. The charge and citations were later dismissed, and a later internal-affairs investigation found body-camera footage did not support an officer's claim that a handgun was in plain view in the cupholder.

Rincon sued under federal civil-rights law, alleging false arrest and an unconstitutional search and seizure connected to his detention and arrest, the search of his vehicle, and the seizure of firearms. The appeals court, in a ruling issued Thursday, Oct. 22, did not decide whether the curfew actually applied to Rincon. Instead, it held that a reasonable officer could have believed it applied, giving at least arguable probable cause for the curfew arrest and thus supporting immunity on the false-arrest claims. It likewise treated the vehicle search and impound and inventory reasoning — based on the holstered weapon and Rincon's statement about additional weapons — as supporting immunity. Even accepting Rincon's disputed versions of certain facts, including that he had not driven into the lot at high speed and that the handgun was not in plain view, the court said the qualified-immunity outcome did not change. The City of Laredo had previously been dismissed from the case by the district court.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “Appeals court upholds immunity for Laredo police officers sued over COVID-19 curfew arrest in 2021,” Oct. 24, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: The 5th Circuit upheld qualified immunity for three Laredo officers sued by Ismael Rincon over a February 2021 COVID curfew arrest, holding a reasonable officer could have believed the curfew applied.
title: Appeals court upholds immunity for Laredo officers sued over 2021 COVID curfew arrest
